title: Apex Predator
desc: Evolutionary arms races, parasitic nightmares & ecosystems on the edge

questions.q: The cordyceps fungus takes over an ant's brain and forces it to climb to a specific height before killing it. Why that exact height?
questions.a: Optimal temperature and humidity for the fungus to grow a spore-releasing stalk from the ant's head — maximising spore dispersal onto ants below

questions.q: What is a 'lazarus taxon' in biology?
questions.a: A species that disappears from the fossil record for a long period then reappears — named after the biblical figure who rose from the dead (e.g. coelacanths)

questions.q: The Yellowstone supervolcano's last major eruption was 640,000 years ago. What would happen to the US if it erupted today?
questions.a: Roughly a 1,000 km radius of destruction, ash covering most of the continent, global cooling for years — effectively a civilisation-ending event for North America

questions.q: Why do deep-sea fish often have transparent or red colouring?
questions.a: Red light doesn't penetrate deep water — so red fish are effectively invisible. Transparent fish let light pass through, casting no shadow for predators to detect

questions.q: The 'grandmother hypothesis' in evolutionary biology explains what puzzling human trait?
questions.a: Why women live decades past menopause — the theory suggests grandmothers who helped raise grandchildren increased their descendants' survival rates

questions.q: What is an 'ecological trap' and give one example?
questions.a: When environmental changes make a poor habitat seem attractive — e.g. sea turtles mistaking beachfront lights for moonlight and heading inland instead of to sea

questions.q: Lichen is often described as a symbiotic relationship between two organisms. Why is that now considered an oversimplification?
questions.a: Lichen actually involves at least three partners — a fungus, an alga or cyanobacterium, AND a recently discovered yeast that was hiding in plain sight (identified in 2016)

questions.q: The 'Wood Wide Web' refers to what underground network?
questions.a: Mycorrhizal fungal networks connecting tree roots — trees share nutrients, water, and chemical warning signals through these fungal threads

questions.q: What is 'convergent evolution' and why do sharks and dolphins look similar despite being completely unrelated?
questions.a: Unrelated species independently evolving similar traits due to similar environmental pressures — the streamlined body shape is optimal for fast aquatic movement

questions.q: The axolotl can regenerate limbs, heart tissue, and even parts of its brain. What's the catch that makes it scientifically frustrating?
questions.a: It's critically endangered in the wild (only found in Lake Xochimilco, Mexico) — so studying it in its natural habitat is nearly impossible
